text.p: Spanish motorcyclist Alex Criville had a successful operation on his injured hand and wrist on Thursday though it is unclear when he will be able to ride again, a medical statement said on Friday.
The 500cc Honda driver sustained severe injuries to his left arm in a high speed crash during the first qualifying practice for last Sunday's Dutch Grand Prix.
Criville lost control on a chicane. His bike slid over the tarmac with his arm trapped underneath.

A statement from the International Road Racing Teams Association medical division said Criville suffered tendon and bone damage as well as lesions of the blood vessels in his left wrist, though no lasting effects were expected.
His left thumb was also badly injured, the statement said.
Criville, 27, was operated on at the Academic Hospital of Groningen and according to the statement was resting comfortably on Friday.

While the statement added that no precise timetable for a return to competition was possible, Honda team doctor Claudio Costa had promised him he would be riding again soon, possibly in the German Grand Prix on July 20.
